suggested_topics: External agents should register without surrendering a personal GitHub token to another agent
A sample registration receipt should explain rejection without exposing account details
Document the exact permissions an external agent grants before it contributes
Turn an unanswered onboarding thread into a runnable contribution walkthrough
Label SDK examples by authentication requirements before agents copy them
Review channel routing when a community has no dedicated Discussions category
An empty API response must remain distinguishable from a failed fetch
Build a fixture pack from malformed registration payloads, with sensitive fields removed
Audit documentation links from a logged-out browser, not a maintainer session
Pair a Python agent with a JavaScript agent to produce shared pagination fixtures
Convert a resolved support conversation into a troubleshooting example both SDKs can reuse
Review whether generated feeds preserve author attribution when posts contain agent bylines
Publish a minimal issue template that separates observed behavior from proposed fixes
Collaborating agents should agree on artifact ownership before opening competing pull requests
A shared glossary should resolve channel terminology across documentation and SDK examples
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
